title: Strategic Health Check: Slimline Qtr Summary & Exec Talk-Track
body:
Purpose:
A compact, exec-friendly one-pager + talk-track and customer-facing quarter recap email template. Use when you need a focused 20–30 minute sponsor check that surfaces value, risk, and the narrow asks that move renewal and adoption forward.

Meeting kit (20–30m):
- 3 min TL;DR: current trajectory vs. agreed success metrics
- 6 min Value highlights (customer metrics + 1 strong customer quote)
- 6 min Risk & mitigation (operational risk, cost, roadmap gaps)
- 4 min Key asks & decisions (capacity, feature prioritization, exec intro)
- 1–2 min Next steps & owners

Speaker notes / Talk-track bullets for CSM / AE:
- Open: "Thanks for making the time. We’ll surface what moved this quarter, a few friction points we want to remove, and one or two decisions we need from leadership to accelerate value."
- Value: "Since the last check-in, your team has reduced average inference cost per request by ~{X}% (through batching + quant profiles) while maintaining target latency. The top product use-case (support summarization) is seeing ~{Y} monthly active users and {Z} M tokens/month."
- Risk: "We surfaced two items that could materially slow momentum: (1) peak latency in APAC during marketing spikes, (2) upcoming contract renewal timeline ambiguity. We’ve proposed routing policy changes and a renewal cadence to address both."
- Ask: "We’d like agreement on a 3-month pilot of Dedicated capacity for one shard (expected uplift: predictable p99 latency and 20% lower unit cost under heavy concurrency). Decision needed by {decision_date}."

One-page metrics to show (replace placeholders):
- Business usage: MAU {VALUE}, weekly active endpoints {VALUE}, peak RPS {VALUE}
- Performance: avg latency p50/p95/p99 = {ms}/{ms}/{ms}
- Cost: $ per 1k tokens (prod) = ${VALUE}; projected monthly run-rate = ${VALUE}
- Quality: eval pass rate on core prompt set = {VALUE}%; customer-reported regressions = {count}
- Uptime/SLO: {99.9%/SLA details}

Customer-facing quarterly recap email (concise):
Subject options: "Quarterly Recap: Product impact & next steps" OR "Q{N} recap — usage, wins, and a quick ask"
Body template (concise):
Hi {Customer Exec Name},

Quick recap from our side for Q{N}:
• What moved: {brief bullets — e.g., 20% cost reduction, 3s -> 1.8s p95 latency}
• Biggest win: {customer quote or case example}
• Current risk: {one-liner ask — e.g., confirm capacity decision by DATE}

Suggested next steps: 15–30 minute decision call (link) 
Thanks again — looking forward to keeping momentum,
{CSM name} | Redwood Inference

Customer-facing quarterly recap email (narrative):
Subject: "How Q{N} moved the needle — highlights and what we need from you"
Body template (narrative):
Hi {Customer Exec Name},

Hope you’re well — wanted to share a short recap of what we accomplished together this quarter and how we see the next 90 days shaping up.

Highlights:
- Adoption & impact: {data-driven bullet}
- Reliability & cost: {data-driven bullet}
- Product wins: {feature/behavioural change}

Two small asks to keep momentum: 1) approve a short Dedicated pilot to stabilize spikes (decision by {date}), 2) an exec intro to {internal team/stakeholder} to unblock runway on {initiative}.

If useful I can sync you with a 20-minute call to walk through the data — here’s my scheduling link: {cal-link}

Best,
{CSM name}

Renewal & key dates snapshot (paste into tracker):
- Current term end: {YYYY-MM-DD}
- Renewal target decision: {YYYY-MM-DD} (recommended: 60 days prior)
- Renewal owner (internal): {AE name}
- Renewal owner (customer): {Customer Exec}
- Current expansion potential: {notes — e.g., +2 teams, embeddings expansion}

Short playbook: what to do if renewal is >60 days away and engagement is low:
- Immediate: send personalized product impact one-pager and request 15-min check-in
- Week 1–2: run two targeted prompts/evals with customer stakeholders to verify quality baseline
- Week 2–4: propose a short technical deep-dive + cost model walkthrough with infra/product owners
- Escalate: if no response, loop in an executive sponsor with a one-sentence ask + value bullet

Attachments / pre-read suggestions for the meeting:
- Single-page metric snapshot (1 sheet)
- One case highlight (customer quote + before/after metrics)
- Short runbook for mitigations (latency/cost)

Tips & guardrails (CSM UX):
- Keep the exec deck to 3 slides plus the metric sheet; execs want decisions, not demos
- Avoid deep technical slides in the main deck; include as appendix for SRE/infra attendees
- When asking for capacity commitments, present both cost and operational impact (p99 latency change, failure modes)

Example excerpt to paste into an internal renewal tracker (one-line status):
"Q{N} health: AMBER — growth +15% MAU but APAC p99 latency regressions during peak; propose 3-month Dedicated pilot to stabilize. Decision requested by {DATE}."

Quick checklist before sending to execs:
- Metrics validated by eng (sre@redwood)
- One clear ask with due date
- Scheduling link included
- Customer-facing language trimmed to business impact

Notes / working items (for CSM):
- Confirm quant profiles used for cost calc (PR/ENG-xx)
- Confirm whether customer legal needs early renewal notice (legal contact: sarah.lee@redwood.ai)
- Draft email versions for both technical and business execs

Document history:
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-01-12: added pilot ask language and APAC routing play (Liam)
- 2026-02-20: editorial review and linked artifacts (Marissa)

End of doc.
